producer_report.summary:
I added `check_design_existing_code` to the reading gate. It refuses a design reading unless it has an `Existing code:` assumption naming a `crates/` or `docs/` path the job does not create, and a criterion that requires an existing code section that reuses or extends it. A criterion is refused when the words "existing code section" are not followed by a reuse or extend word within 12 words. It is also refused when a negator (no, not, never, without, nothing, nor, cannot) sits from 3 words before the phrase through that reuse word. So "no survey needed" and "the existing code in section 3 is unchanged" are refused. The check reads only the reading and skips other classes, readings with a question, and declines.

The step runs in `refusing_check` right after `check_code_survey`. The root cause is that nothing asked for an inventory of existing code before a design was accepted.

I also made these changes:
- **Reader brief:** `READING_RULES` now has six lines. The new one teaches the rule and names `check_design_existing_code`, so a correct reading passes on the first read.
- **Corpus:** `refusal_corpus.rs` has a `design-existing-code` input form (16 in total), four design cases, and a declared-intended test.
- **Changelog:** `CHANGELOG.md` has an entry with the intended refusal rate, "expected 5% of newly refused readings".

I ran the targeted tests for athena-core, the refusal corpus, athena-context, the athena-cli budgets and the xtask policy scan, plus fmt and clippy. All pass. I did not run the whole-workspace `cargo test`.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: unit tests in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs show a design reading with an `Existing code:` assumption naming a path that is not a create deliverable, and a criterion requiring an Existing code section that reuses or extends it, is accepted. They fail without the change.
criteria_check.evidence: design_existing_code_compliant_reading_is_accepted passed in `cargo test -p athena-core` (742 passed). It accepts four criterion wordings and a lower-case, trimmed label with a backticked path. It also asserts refusing_check names check_design_existing_code once the assumption is removed. Without the change the test does not compile and the step name does not exist.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a design reading whose criterion contains 'existing code' and 'section' but says the opposite (for example 'no survey needed' or 'the existing code in section 3 is unchanged') is refused.
criteria_check.evidence: design_existing_code_opposite_criteria_are_refused passed. It refuses 'no survey needed', 'the existing code in section 3 is unchanged', 'no existing code section is needed, nothing to reuse or extend', a "doesn't" form, the phrase with no reuse word, and a reuse word 13 words after the phrase. Each error contains 'Existing code' and 'existing code section'. A reuse word exactly 12 words after is accepted.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a design reading whose `Existing code:` assumption names only the file the job creates is refused, as is one with no such assumption.
criteria_check.evidence: design_existing_code_names_a_path_the_job_does_not_create passed. It refuses an assumption naming only the Create deliverable, a Code survey: assumption alone, and the label with no path, a bare root, an xtask/ path, or not at the start. The same path as a Modify deliverable is accepted.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: readings of class code, tests, docs and config, and design readings with a question or a decline, are still accepted.
criteria_check.evidence: design_existing_code_does_not_apply_outside_its_gate passed. It asserts accept and a direct check_design_existing_code both Ok for classes code, tests, docs and config, and for a design reading with a question and one with capability None plus a decline_reason. The same design reading without either is refused.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus`: a new case built from a design reading written from request text alone is refused by check_design_existing_code, is declared intended, and the guard that every step! has a refusing case passes.
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` passed 7/7. It runs three new refusing design cases (no assumption, created file only, opposite criterion) and one accepting case, all tagged design-existing-code (INPUT_FORMS now 16). It also runs every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case and design_existing_code_refusal_is_declared_intended.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-context`: READING_RULES has six lines, one naming `Existing code:` and `check_design_existing_code`; the line-count, per-line 220-byte, section under 2400 bytes, every-check-has-a-rule-line and budget tests pass.
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo test -p athena-context` passed 93/93. READING_RULES is now [&str; 6]. The extended the_reader_brief_names_each_reading_rule_in_one_short_line asserts six lines, a line holding both `Existing code:` and `check_design_existing_code`, each line at most 220 bytes, the check name in the section, and the section under 2400 bytes. athena-cli budgets test also passed.

criteria_check.criterion: Grep of crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs shows `step!(check_design_existing_code(reading));` in refusing_check, and a doc comment without blank lines naming the root cause (no inventory of existing code before a design is accepted) and jobs 20261026-043137-zc0v and 20261026-065046-0c1d; the refusal text names the `Existing code:` label and what to list.
criteria_check.evidence: The step line sits directly after step!(check_code_survey(reading)); in refusing_check. The doc comment is `///` lines with none blank and names the root cause and both job ids. The refusal text says to add an assumption that starts `Existing code:` and lists the crates/ or docs/ files, functions and docs the design changes or reuses, not the files the job creates. design_existing_code_refusal_is_declared_intended (reading.rs and refusal_corpus.rs) asserts these facts and passed.

The corpus test asserts replay_declaration reads share Some(5) and that the changelog holds the phrases.

open_issues: The 5% share is the brief's estimate. records/ is absent, so I ran no replay and it is unmeasured.
The check accepts only crates/ and docs/ paths, as the brief fixes. A design that touches only xtask/ or athena.toml is refused.
The doc comment names jobs 20261026-043137-zc0v and 20261026-065046-0c1d as design jobs accepted without an inventory. This rests on the brief; I could not read those jobs' records.
I did not run the full workspace `cargo test`; Athena's check covers it.
mistakes: My first rule line was 226 bytes, over the 220-byte limit. I shortened it before running the tests.
I first wrote the doc comment without `///` prefixes. I fixed it before compiling.
learnings: The reading-rule line limit of 220 bytes counts the `- ` prefix, so the line text is at most 218 bytes.
The existing code-survey doc-comment test splits reading.rs on `pub fn check_code_survey`, so the new function and its comment must not contain that string.
READING_RULES is outside BudgetSet::Reader, so the rule line needs no token headroom.
desires: A way to read large saved tool output inside the working directory, since Grep refuses a path outside it.
Records for a measured replay of the 5% share.
